title: Israeli forces demolish four water wells, greenhouses in Hebron
summary:
Israeli forces demolish four water wells, greenhouses in Hebron

Israeli forces demolished four water wells and several greenhouses on Wednesday in the Al-Thaghra neighborhood of Beit Ummar, north of Hebron in the occupied West Bank, Wafa news reported.

Citing a local source, Wafa said that Israeli forces used a bulldozer to demolish four water wells in the al-Thaghra area, each reaching approximately 40 meters underground, which were used to irrigate crops and for other agricultural purposes.

Israeli soldiers also reportedly demolished several greenhouses in the same area, claiming they lacked permits.

title: Turkey replaces Russian oil and diesel imports from US as wars reverberate
summary:
Turkey replaces Russian oil and diesel imports from US as wars reverberate

Turkey is turning to the United States for crude oil and refined products as supplies from Russia are jolted amid increasing Ukrainian attacks on its energy infrastructure, according to recent Turkish customs data.

The US overtook Russia in June as Turkey’s main crude oil supplier with roughly 570,000 tonnes arriving compared to 425,000 from Russia. The numbers reflect how Ankara is reducing its exposure to Russian crude after emerging as one of its top buyers following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Turkey’s cut in Russian crude oil imports also comes as it purchases more diesel from the US and India.

According to energy analytics firm Kpler, Turkey has imported more than 120,000 barrels per day of Indian diesel and 90,000 bpd of diesel from the US since August. The volumes were the highest on record, according to Kpler data starting in 2017.

title: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran
summary:
'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said it "wouldn't be appropriate to say" if he would greenlight the CIA arming Iranians to encourage a violent uprising, a day after he asked on his TruthSocial account, "When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?"

Trump was taking unscheduled questions in the Oval Office, after the US unleashed a barrage of strikes on Iran's southern coast on Tuesday, killing 18 people, including two children at a wedding. 

"Will you send the CIA in to arm Iranians?" a reporter asked the president.

"I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say," Trump responded. "But I mean, I understand their plight. They're being shot... They have close to 65,000 protesters killed."

It remains unclear where that figure is sourced, given Trump has previously floated figures between 25,000 and 80,000 during the anti-government protests in Iran early this year. 

Iran's own figure is about 3,800 killed. 

Read more: 'Inappropriate to say': Trump may still be considering CIA-led uprising in Iran

title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
summary:
Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever.

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

summary:
Israeli military announces military exercise in occupied West Bank

The Israeli army have announced on Wednesday that troops will take part in a military exercise in the northern occupied West Bank area on Thursday.

“As part of the exercise, there will be noticeable active movement of security forces in the area. There is no fear of a security incident,” the military said in a statement to social media.

The activity is set to take place in the Ephraim and Menashe Brigade areas, which include cities and villages such as Jenin, Tuba, and Tulkarem “starting from the morning hours until noon”.

title: Half of Americans think post-9/11 wars were worth it, poll shows
summary:
Half of Americans think post-9/11 wars were worth it, poll shows

Submitted by Yasmine El-Sabawi on Wed, 09/02/2026 - 16:43
The same number of people seem to agree that Muslims are the worst-treated group in the United States
Pedestrians standing on the Brooklyn waterfront look across the East River towards the burning twin towers of the World Trade Center in lower Manhattan, New York on 11 September 2001 (Henny Ray Abrams/AFP)
Off

Nearly half of Americans believe their country's military operations and surveillance infrastructure that followed the 11 September 2001 attacks have been "worth it", according to a YouGov poll published on Wednesday.

Nearly the same amount also believe that Muslims have been the most mistreated group since the attacks, the results showed. 

The questions come ahead of the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks on the World Trade Center buildings in New York City, after four planes were hijacked and two of them flown into the towers.

The third plane crashed into the Pentagon in Washington, DC, and the fourth in a field in Pennsylvania. 

Asked if fighting "against the threat of terrorism through military operations abroad" and introducing "increased security and surveillance inside of the United States... have been worth the cost", 48 percent of respondents said yes, while another 27 percent said they weren't sure. The remaining 25 percent said no. 

Divided by political leaning, far more Republicans than Democrats said yes - nearly double the amount at 71 percent.

Five years after the fall of Kabul, 'war on terror' ghosts have come home
Read More »

In the immediate aftermath of 9/11, then-President George W Bush created the Department of Homeland Security, ushering in the Transportation Security Administration, which is the body that makes travelers take off their shoes, separate their laptops from their bags and empty out their liquids before flying. 

Bush also signed the Patriot Act into law, which brought in sweeping authorisation to track phone calls and movements of American citizens.

The 2001 Authorisation for the Use of Military Force, passed by Congress, remains active to this day and has been used for unlimited US military attacks on several sovereign nations, including Afghanistan, Somalia, Syria and Pakistan. 

YouGov surveyed 1,098 US citizens over the age of 18 through a web-based survey between 20-23 August. 

The margin of error is +/- 4.1 points.

Islamophobia

Just under half of respondents said the US is safer now than it was before 9/11.

Among Republican respondents, that figure was 60 percent. Only 20 percent said the US is now less safe.

"It stems from the propaganda," Maha Hilal, author of the book Innocent Until Proven Muslim, which documents the impact of the "war on terror" told Middle East Eye.

"I think it's pretty easy to convince people that they're safer now because of their ability to maintain the same sort of lifestyle, especially as Americans tend to be quite apathetic anyway," she said.

"Their ability to maintain the same sort of lifestyle post-9/11 and in the 'war on terror' has, I think, been relatively unchanged."

When the pollsters asked if "Muslims in the United States have been treated better, about the same, or worse than people of other religions", 52 percent of respondents said Muslims have been treated worse.

Among Democrats, that figure is 71 percent, whereas among Republicans it lands at 28 percent. Independents fell squarely in between. 

The figures largely reflect the current views and narratives coming from each side of the aisle, as Republicans ramp up the kind of anti-Muslim rhetoric that both elders and experts in the Muslim community have said is much worse than the immediate post-9/11 climate. 

Asked "which kind of perpetrator has committed the greatest number of violent attacks in the US", a quarter of all respondents pointed to right-wing extremists, while 19 percent said it's "Islamic extremists".

Another 17 percent said it was "lone wolves who aren’t affiliated with any particular group or ideology", while 13 percent pointed to left-wing extremists.

Old playbook

Key to the "war on terror" narrative is longevity, Hilal told MEE.

"It has been to reiterate over and over again how this war has been a success, and how it has stopped numerous acts of terrorism," she said. 

Even among "leftists and liberals", she noted, it has been difficult "to communicate the idea that Islamophobia has been a part and parcel to the war.

"The targeting of Muslims is usually treated as an unintended consequence."

This week, CBS News faced internal backlash over its coverage of Muslim US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, with current and former staffers accusing the network of poor journalism and “overt” racism.

The controversy erupted after CBS published a story highlighting old social media posts by El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee in Michigan for the US Senate, ahead of the 25th anniversary of 9/11.

CBS staff accuse network of ‘overt racism’ over Abdul El-Sayed 9/11 story
Read More »

El-Sayed, who could become the first Muslim elected to the Senate this November, had deleted posts in which he compared the mounting Covid-19 death toll with the nearly 3,000 people killed on 11 September 2001 and called for Washington to mobilise against poverty and the pandemic as it had after the attacks.

“We could save lives rather than take them,” he wrote.

More than one million Americans died of Covid-19-related causes. 

Another post by Sayed mourned those killed on 9/11 as well as those killed during the wars that followed - and that figure is staggering.

A research report from the Costs of War project at Brown University’s Watson Institute in 2023 estimated that 4.5 million people have died as a consequence of wars in the Middle East, North Africa and Asia since the 9/11 attacks.

Of the 4.5 million fatalities, there were at least 3.6 to 3.7 million "indirect" deaths caused by a variety of factors.

The categories in the report are economic collapse and food insecurity; public services and health infrastructure destruction; environmental contamination; reverberating trauma and violence; and other impacts.

The US invaded Afghanistan and drove the Taliban from power in retaliation for the 9/11 attacks, which had been planned while al-Qaeda's leader, Osama bin Laden, was living in the country under Taliban protection. The Taliban, however, returned to power in Afghanistan as the US withdrew from the country in 2021.

The number of deaths caused by post-9/11 conflicts has been a source of intense controversy, as politics and inexact science have intersected in heated debates of conflicting interests. 

In 2015, the Nobel Prize-winning Physicians for Social Responsibility estimated that more than one million people had been killed both directly and indirectly in the wars in Iraq, Afghanistan and Pakistan alone.

According to the Cost of Wars report, which looks at the cost of war across conflicts in Afghanistan, Pakistan, Iraq, Syria, Libya, Somalia and Yemen, indirect deaths grew in scale over time. 

Though the US withdrew its military forces from Afghanistan in 2021, officially ending the war, Afghans are “suffering and dying from war-related causes at higher rates than ever”.

“Indirect deaths are devastating, not least because so many of them could be prevented, were it not for war,” the report said.

title: Israel’s mission in Iran ‘not yet finished’, says Netanyahu
summary:
Israel’s mission in Iran ‘not yet finished’, says Netanyahu

Israel’s mission in Iran is “not yet finished”, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Israeli media on Wednesday, adding that the intention is to “bring it down”.

“All of our systems under my direction are working to overthrow this regime,” Netanyahu told i24News.

This comes after Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz and Foreign Minister Gideon Saar both threatened that Israel would respond heavily to any Iranian attack.

title: Two Palestinian teenagers killed by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank
summary:
Two Palestinian teenagers killed by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank

Two Palestinian teenagers were killed by Israeli forces and settlers on Wednesday evening during an attack on the village of al-Mughayyir, north of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, Wafa news reported.

The Palestinian Red Crescent Society said its crews evacuated two 19-year-old Palestinians, who were shot with live ammunition, one in the neck and the other in the back, during an attack by settlers and Israeli forces on the village.

They later succumbed to their injuries after being transported to hospital.
